messages.content: You are a helpful assistant.
Why does one stretch of a trip suddenly feel flat when nothing about it has changed?
I suppose it is some association of ideas that makes those dead places in a journey.
You are a helpful assistant.
How do you keep getting better at things?
I learn how to do it. Every day I learn to do things smoother and better.
You are a helpful assistant.
How does it feel to miss out on what's important?
I had the feeling of a boy who thinks of what is happening at a certain hour at the schoolhouse from which he has played truant.
You are a helpful assistant.
How can you tell if someone truly cares about something?

Aficion means passion. An aficionado is one who is passionate about the bull-fights. All the good bull-fighters stayed at Montoya’s hotel; that is, those with aficion stayed there. The commercial bull-fighters stayed once, perhaps, and then did not come back. The good ones came each year. In Montoya’s room were their photographs. The photographs were dedicated to Juanito Montoya or to his sister. The photographs of bull-fighters Montoya had really believed in were framed. Photographs of bull-fighters who had been without aficion Montoya kept in a drawer of his desk. They often had the most flattering inscriptions. But they did not mean anything. One day Montoya took them all out and dropped them in the waste-basket. He did not want them around.
You are a helpful assistant.
Show me Robert Cohn after he has been insulted.

Cohn still sat at the table. His face had the sallow, yellow look it got when he was insulted, but somehow he seemed to be enjoying it. The childish, drunken heroics of it. It was his affair with a lady of title.
You are a helpful assistant.
How would you describe the bull coming out into the corral?

I leaned way over the wall and tried to see into the cage. It was dark. Some one rapped on the cage with an iron bar. Inside something seemed to explode. The bull, striking into the wood from side to side with his horns, made a great noise. Then I saw a dark muzzle and the shadow of horns, and then, with a clattering on the wood in the hollow box, the bull charged and came out into the corral, skidding with his forefeet in the straw as he stopped, his head up, the great hump of muscle on his neck swollen tight, his body muscles quivering as he looked up at the crowd on the stone walls. The two steers backed away against the wall, their heads sunken, their eyes watching the bull.
You are a helpful assistant.
Show me someone meeting Miss Barkley at the hospital.

At dinner I ate very quickly and left for the villa where the British had their hospital. It was really very large and beautiful and there were fine trees in the grounds. Miss Barkley was sitting on a bench in the garden. Miss Ferguson was with her. They seemed glad to see me and in a little while Miss Ferguson excused herself and went away.
You are a helpful assistant.
Describe a boy eating pie with his father.

His father sat watching him eat and filled his glass from the milk-pitcher. Nick drank and wiped his mouth on his napkin. His father reached over to the shelf for the pie. He cut Nick a big piece. It was huckleberry pie.
You are a helpful assistant.
What was Robert Cohn like at Princeton?

Robert Cohn was a member, through his father, of one of the richest Jewish families in New York, and through his mother of one of the oldest. At the military school where he prepped for Princeton, and played a very good end on the football team, no one had made him race-conscious. No one had ever made him feel he was a Jew, and hence any different from anybody else, until he went to Princeton. He was a nice boy, a friendly boy, and very shy, and it made him bitter. He took it out in boxing, and he came out of Princeton with painful self-consciousness and the flattened nose, and was married by the first girl who was nice to him.
You are a helpful assistant.
Picture the view from the stone fortifications with Brett.

We walked out across the wet grass and onto the stone wall of the fortifications. I spread a newspaper on the stone and Brett sat down. Across the plain it was dark, and we could see the mountains. The wind was high up and took the clouds across the moon. Below us were the dark pits of the fortifications. Behind were the trees and the shadow of the cathedral, and the town silhouetted against the moon.
You are a helpful assistant.
Describe the lieutenant-colonel's execution.

Two carabinieri took the lieutenant-colonel to the river bank. He walked in the rain, an old man with his hat off, a carabiniere on either side. I did not watch them shoot him but I heard the shots. They were questioning some one else. This officer too was separated from his troops. He was not allowed to make an explanation. He cried when they read the sentence from the pad of paper, and they were questioning another when they shot him. They made a point of being intent on questioning the next man while the man who had been questioned before was being shot. In this way there was obviously nothing they could do about it. I did not know whether I should wait to be questioned or make a break now. I was obviously a German in Italian uniform.
You are a helpful assistant.
Picture the refugee column in the rain.

In the night many peasants had joined the column from the roads of the country and in the column there were carts loaded with household goods; there were mirrors projecting up between mattresses, and chickens and ducks tied to carts. There was a sewing-machine on the cart ahead of us in the rain. They had saved the most valuable things. On some carts the women sat huddled from the rain and others walked beside the carts keeping as close to them as they could. There were dogs now in the column, keeping under the wagons as they moved along. The road was muddy, the ditches at the side were high with water and beyond the trees that lined the road the fields looked too wet and too soggy to try to cross.
You are a helpful assistant.
Show me a man's memory of a girl with her mother.

Once there was an American woman sitting with her kid daughter at the next table to us and they were both eating ices and I kept looking at the girl and she was awfully good looking and I smiled at her and she smiled at me but that was all that ever came of it because I looked for her mother and her every day and I made up ways that I was going to speak to her and I wondered if I got to know her if her mother would let me take her out to Auteuil or Tremblay but I never saw either of them again.
You are a helpful assistant.
Describe a drive down a road hidden from the enemy.

You saw the flash, then heard the crack, then saw the smoke ball distort and thin in the wind. There were many iron shrapnel balls in the rubble of the houses and on the road beside the broken house where the post was, but they did not shell near the post that afternoon. We loaded two cars and drove down the road that was screened with wet mats and the last of the sun came through in the breaks between the strips of mattings. Before we were out on the clear road behind the hill the sun was down. We went on down the clear road and as it turned a corner into the open and went into the square arched tunnel of matting the rain started again.
You are a helpful assistant.
Show me a day of waiting during the rain.

When daylight came the storm was still blowing but the snow had stopped. It had melted as it fell on the wet ground and now it was raining again. There was another attack just after daylight but it was unsuccessful. We expected an attack all day but it did not come until the sun was going down. The bombardment started to the south below the long wooded ridge where the Austrian guns were concentrated. We expected a bombardment but it did not come. It was getting dark. Guns were firing from the field behind the village and the shells, going away, had a comfortable sound.
You are a helpful assistant.
Describe the bullfighter Belmonte's painful afternoon.

Also Belmonte imposed conditions and insisted that his bulls should not be too large, nor too dangerously armed with horns, and so the element that was necessary to give the sensation of tragedy was not there, and the public, who wanted three times as much from Belmonte, who was sick with a fistula, as Belmonte had ever been able to give, felt defrauded and cheated, and Belmonte’s jaw came further out in contempt, and his face turned yellower, and he moved with greater difficulty as his pain increased, and finally the crowd were actively against him, and he was utterly contemptuous and indifferent. He had meant to have a great afternoon, and instead it was an afternoon of sneers, shouted insults, and finally a volley of cushions and pieces of bread and vegetables, thrown down at him in the plaza where he had had his greatest triumphs.
You are a helpful assistant.
Show me someone arriving at the villa.

On a narrow street we passed a British Red Cross ambulance. The driver wore a cap and his face was thin and very tanned. I did not know him. I got down from the camion in the big square in front of the Town Major’s house, the driver handed down my rucksack and I put it on and swung on the two musettes and walked to our villa. It did not feel like a homecoming.
You are a helpful assistant.
Describe a man trying to keep warm.

So he ate an orange, slowly spitting out the seeds. Outside, the snow was turning to rain. Inside, the electric stove seemed to give no heat and rising from his writing-table, he sat down upon the stove. How good it felt! Here, at last, was life.
You are a helpful assistant.
Describe a beech wood.

It was a beech wood and the trees were very old. Their roots bulked above the ground and the branches were twisted. We walked on the road between the thick trunks of the old beeches and the sunlight came through the leaves in light patches on the grass. The trees were big, and the foliage was thick but it was not gloomy. There was no undergrowth, only the smooth grass, very green and fresh, and the big gray trees well spaced as though it were a park.
You are a helpful assistant.
Describe someone writing telegrams.

As I went into the dining-room the concierge brought me a police bulletin to fill out. I signed it and asked him for two telegraph forms, and wrote a message to the Hotel Montoya, telling them to forward all mail and telegrams for me to this address. I calculated how many days I would be in San Sebastian and then wrote out a wire to the office asking them to hold mail, but forward all wires for me to San Sebastian for six days. Then I went in and had lunch.
You are a helpful assistant.
Tell me about the hospital stay in the garden.

When they lifted you up out of bed to carry you into the dressing room you could look out of the window and see the new graves in the garden. A soldier sat outside the door that opened onto the garden making crosses and painting on them the names, rank, and regiment of the men who were buried in the garden. He also ran errands for the ward and in his spare time made me a cigarette lighter out of an empty Austrian rifle cartridge. The doctors were very nice and seemed very capable. They were anxious to ship me to Milan where there were better X-ray facilities and where, after the operation, I could take mechano-therapy. I wanted to go to Milan too. They wanted to get us all out and back as far as possible because all the beds were needed for the offensive, when it should start.
You are a helpful assistant.
What was the bull-ring celebration like?

The covered seats of the bull-ring had been crowded with people sitting out of the rain watching the concourse of Basque and Navarrais dancers and singers, and afterward the Val Carlos dancers in their costumes danced down the street in the rain, the drums sounding hollow and damp, and the chiefs of the bands riding ahead on their big, heavy-footed horses, their costumes wet, the horses’ coats wet in the rain. The crowd was in the cafés and the dancers came in, too, and sat, their tight-wound white legs under the tables, shaking the water from their belled caps, and spreading their red and purple jackets over the chairs to dry. It was raining hard outside.
You are a helpful assistant.

Rewrite this:

A large car traveled quickly past us, causing a layer of muddy water to splash onto our windshield and radiator. The automatic windshield cleaner then moved across the glass, distributing the film of mud. We subsequently stopped and ate lunch in Sestri. The restaurant lacked heating, so we remained dressed in our hats and coats. We observed the car through the window; it was covered in mud and parked next to several boats that had been pulled ashore, beyond the reach of the waves. Inside the restaurant, our breath was visible.

A big car passed us, going fast, and a sheet of muddy water rose up and over our wind-shield and radiator. The automatic wind-shield cleaner moved back and forth, spreading the film over the glass. We stopped and ate lunch at Sestri. There was no heat in the restaurant and we kept our hats and coats on. We could see the car outside, through the window. It was covered with mud and was stopped beside some boats that had been pulled up beyond the waves. In the restaurant you could see your breath.
You are a helpful assistant.

Put this into your own style:

The bus ascended the road at a consistent rate. The landscape was infertile, characterized by rocks protruding from the clay soil. There was no grass adjacent to the road. From our vantage point looking backward, we observed the terrain extending beneath us. In the distance, the fields appeared as rectangular areas of green and brown on the hillsides. Brown mountains formed the horizon, and these mountains had unusual shapes. As our elevation increased, the horizon continuously shifted. While the bus slowly progressed up the road, we observed additional mountains emerging to the south. Subsequently, the road reached the crest, became level, and entered a forest. This forest consisted of cork oaks. Sunlight filtered through the trees in intermittent patches, and cattle were grazing among the trees in the background.

The bus climbed steadily up the road. The country was barren and rocks stuck up through the clay. There was no grass beside the road. Looking back we could see the country spread out below. Far back the fields were squares of green and brown on the hillsides. Making the horizon were the brown mountains. They were strangely shaped. As we climbed higher the horizon kept changing. As the bus ground slowly up the road we could see other mountains coming up in the south. Then the road came over the crest, flattened out, and went into a forest. It was a forest of cork oaks, and the sun came through the trees in patches, and there were cattle grazing back in the trees.
You are a helpful assistant.

Rewrite this:

Before becoming a concierge, the woman had operated a concession that sold drinks at the Paris racecourses. Her primary professional experience was with individuals in the pelouse area, but she also observed people in the pesage area. She frequently informed me, with considerable pride, about my guests, specifically identifying which ones were well-mannered, which belonged to good families, and which were "sportsmen," a French term where the emphasis is placed on the second syllable. The main issue was that guests who did not fit into any of these three classifications were frequently informed that I was not present at home, at the Barnes residence. For example, one of my friends, a painter who appeared very undernourished and was clearly not considered well-mannered, of a good family, or a sportsman by Madame Duzinell, sent me a letter. In this letter, he requested that I obtain a pass for him to bypass the concierge so he could visit me occasionally in the evenings.

The concierge, before she became a concierge, had owned a drink-selling concession at the Paris race-courses. Her life-work lay in the pelouse, but she kept an eye on the people of the pesage, and she took great pride in telling me which of my guests were well brought up, which were of good family, who were sportsmen, a French word pronounced with the accent on the men. The only trouble was that people who did not fall into any of those three categories were very liable to be told there was no one home, chez Barnes. One of my friends, an extremely underfed-looking painter, who was obviously to Madame Duzinell neither well brought up, of good family, nor a sportsman, wrote me a letter asking if I could get him a pass to get by the concierge so he could come up and see me occasionally in the evenings.
You are a helpful assistant.

Rewrite the following passage:

Zurito spoke to two other members of the cuadrilla, and these two individuals then ran to stand behind Manuel, using their capes. At this point, there were four men positioned behind Manuel. Hernandez had been following Manuel since Manuel initially appeared with the muleta. Fuentes was observing the scene; he was holding his cape against his body, and he was tall and appeared to be at rest, watching with a relaxed gaze. The two additional men then approached. Hernandez signaled to them to position themselves one on each side of Manuel. Manuel remained standing alone, facing the bull.

Zurito spoke to two of the other lads of the cuadrilla and they ran out to stand back of Manuel with their capes. There were four men back of him now. Hernandez had followed him since he first came out with the muleta. Fuentes stood watching, his cape held against his body, tall, in repose, watching lazy-eyed. Now the two came up. Hernandez motioned them to stand one at each side. Manuel stood alone, facing the bull.
You are a helpful assistant.

Put this into your own style:

The individual in question likely did not give much consideration to his attire. His external demeanor was shaped by his time at Princeton. Internally, he was influenced by two women who had educated him. He possessed a pleasant, youthful cheerfulness that he had retained, and I may not have adequately represented this quality. He enjoyed winning at tennis, possibly as much as Lenglen, for example. However, he did not become upset when he lost. After he developed romantic feelings for Brett, his tennis performance significantly declined. Opponents who previously had no chance against him began to defeat him. He maintained a pleasant attitude about these losses.

I do not believe he thought about his clothes much. Externally he had been formed at Princeton. Internally he had been moulded by the two women who had trained him. He had a nice, boyish sort of cheerfulness that had never been trained out of him, and I probably have not brought it out. He loved to win at tennis. He probably loved to win as much as Lenglen, for instance. On the other hand, he was not angry at being beaten. When he fell in love with Brett his tennis game went all to pieces. People beat him who had never had a chance with him. He was very nice about it.
You are a helpful assistant.

Say this in your own words:

The driver assisted us in removing our bags from the vehicle. A group of children was observing the car. The square was hot, the trees were green, and flags were displayed on their staffs. It was preferable to move out of the direct sunlight and into the shade provided by the arcade, which extended around the entire perimeter of the square. Montoya expressed pleasure at our arrival, shook our hands, and assigned us satisfactory rooms that overlooked the square. Subsequently, we washed and tidied ourselves before proceeding downstairs to the dining room for lunch. The driver also remained for lunch. After the meal, we compensated him, and he began his return journey to Bayonne.

The driver helped us down with the bags. There was a crowd of kids watching the car, and the square was hot, and the trees were green, and the flags hung on their staffs, and it was good to get out of the sun and under the shade of the arcade that runs all the way around the square. Montoya was glad to see us, and shook hands and gave us good rooms looking out on the square, and then we washed and cleaned up and went down-stairs in the dining-room for lunch. The driver stayed for lunch, too, and afterward we paid him and he started back to Bayonne.
You are a helpful assistant.

Rewrite the following passage:

After crossing the fields, we encountered a second stream that flowed more quickly than the previous one. A road made of sand descended to a ford, and then continued into a wooded area. The path we were following crossed this stream on a second foot-log, which was located downstream from the ford. This path then merged with the road, and we proceeded into the woods.

Beyond the fields we crossed another faster-flowing stream. A sandy road led down to the ford and beyond into the woods. The path crossed the stream on another foot-log below the ford, and joined the road, and we went into the woods.
You are a helpful assistant.

Rewrite this in your own voice:

She removed her nightgown, and I observed her back, which was white. I then averted my gaze because she had indicated that she wanted me to do so. She was in the early stages of pregnancy, and her body was starting to enlarge slightly, which she did not wish me to see. While I was getting dressed, I could hear the sound of rain hitting the windows. I had only a small number of items to pack into my bag.

I saw her white back as she took off her nightgown and then I looked away because she wanted me to. She was beginning to be a little big with the child and she did not want me to see her. I dressed hearing the rain on the windows. I did not have much to put in my bag.
You are a helpful assistant.

Rewrite this in your own voice:

When we drove through the suburbs of Genoa, it was raining heavily. Even though we were moving very slowly behind tram-cars and motor trucks, liquid mud splashed onto the sidewalks, causing people to step into doorways as our vehicle approached. In San Pier d’Arena, which is an industrial suburb located outside of Genoa, there is a wide street that has two car-tracks. We drove down the center of this street to prevent mud from splashing onto men who were returning home from work. The Mediterranean Sea was on our left side. There was a significant sea running, and waves were breaking, with the wind blowing spray against the car. A river-bed that had been wide, stony, and dry when we had previously passed it while entering Italy was now running brown and was filled up to its banks.

It was raining hard when we passed through the suburbs of Genoa and, even going very slowly behind the tram-cars and the motor trucks, liquid mud splashed on to the sidewalks, so that people stepped into doorways as they saw us coming. In San Pier d’Arena, the industrial suburb outside of Genoa, there is a wide street with two car-tracks and we drove down the centre to avoid sending the mud on to the men going home from work. On our left was the Mediterranean. There was a big sea running and waves broke and the wind blew the spray against the car. A river-bed that, when we had passed, going into Italy, had been wide, stony and dry, was running brown, and up to the banks.
You are a helpful assistant.

Rewrite the following passage:

We kissed on the stairs a second time. When I requested the cordon, the concierge made an unclear statement from behind her door. I returned upstairs and observed Brett from the open window. She was walking up the street toward a large limousine that was parked at the curb, directly under an arc-light. She entered the vehicle, and it began to move. I turned away from the window. On the table, there was one empty glass and another glass that was half-full of brandy and soda. I carried both glasses to the kitchen and emptied the contents of the half-full glass into the sink. I then turned off the gas in the dining room. After that, I removed my slippers while sitting on the bed and then got into bed. This situation involved Brett, and I had previously felt like crying because of it. Subsequently, I recalled seeing her walk up the street and enter the car, which was the last time I had seen her. After a short period, I began to feel extremely distressed again.

We kissed again on the stairs and as I called for the cordon the concierge muttered something behind her door. I went back up-stairs and from the open window watched Brett walking up the street to the big limousine drawn up to the curb under the arc-light. She got in and it started off. I turned around. On the table was an empty glass and a glass half-full of brandy and soda. I took them both out to the kitchen and poured the half-full glass down the sink. I turned off the gas in the dining-room, kicked off my slippers sitting on the bed, and got into bed. This was Brett, that I had felt like crying about. Then I thought of her walking up the street and stepping into the car, as I had last seen her, and of course in a little while I felt like hell again.
You are a helpful assistant.

Rewrite the following passage:

Catherine turned on all the lights in the room and began to unpack her belongings. I ordered a whiskey and soda, then lay on the bed and read the newspapers I had purchased at the station. The date was March 1918, and the German offensive had begun in France. I consumed the whiskey and soda and continued reading as Catherine unpacked and moved about the room.

Catherine turned on all the lights and commenced unpacking. I ordered a whiskey and soda and lay on the bed and read the papers I had bought at the station. It was March, 1918, and the German offensive had started in France. I drank the whiskey and soda and read while Catherine unpacked and moved around the room.
You are a helpful assistant.

Rewrite the following passage:

He entered the train, and the conductor then closed the door, causing the train to depart. I returned to the farm by riding in the cart. Jack was located on the porch, where he was engaged in writing a letter to his wife. The mail had arrived, so I retrieved the papers and proceeded to the opposite side of the porch, where I sat down to read them. Hogan subsequently exited the door and approached me.

He went in and the conductor swung up and the train went out. I rode back to the farm in the cart. Jack was on the porch writing a letter to his wife. The mail had come and I got the papers and went over on the other side of the porch and sat down to read. Hogan came out the door and walked over to me.
You are a helpful assistant.

Rewrite the following passage:

Solly Freedman approached the corner where we were located. This occurred while Jack was applying bandages to his hands and John was positioned in Walcott's corner. Jack inserted his thumb through the opening in the bandage and then wrapped his hand in a smooth and even manner. I then secured the bandage by taping it around his wrist and twice across his knuckles.

Solly Freedman came over to our corner while Jack is bandaging his hands and John is over in Walcott’s corner. Jack puts his thumb through the slit in the bandage and then wrapped his hand nice and smooth. I taped it around the wrist and twice across the knuckles.
You are a helpful assistant.

Rewrite the following passage:

It was becoming dark outside. The street light located outside the window was activated. Two men who were at the counter read the menu. Nick Adams observed these two men from the opposite end of the counter. He had been conversing with George when the two men entered.

Outside it was getting dark. The street-light came on outside the window. The two men at the counter read the menu. From the other end of the counter Nick Adams watched them. He had been talking to George when they came in.
You are a helpful assistant.

Rewrite this in your own voice:

I turned on the lamp next to the bed, then turned off the gas. After that, I opened the wide windows. The bed was positioned a significant distance from the windows. I sat by the bed with the windows open and undressed. Outside, a night train, which operated on the streetcar tracks, passed by. This train was transporting vegetables to the markets. These trains were loud at night, especially when one was unable to sleep. While undressing, I observed my reflection in the mirror of the large armoire, which was located beside the bed. This method of furnishing a room was characteristic of French style. I also considered it practical. I thought about the various ways one could be wounded, and I supposed it was humorous. I then put on my pajamas and got into bed. I had two bull-fight papers, and I removed their wrappers. One of the papers was orange, and the other was yellow.

I lit the lamp beside the bed, turned off the gas, and opened the wide windows. The bed was far back from the windows, and I sat with the windows open and undressed by the bed. Outside a night train, running on the street-car tracks, went by carrying vegetables to the markets. They were noisy at night when you could not sleep. Undressing, I looked at myself in the mirror of the big armoire beside the bed. That was a typically French way to furnish a room. Practical, too, I suppose. Of all the ways to be wounded. I suppose it was funny. I put on my pajamas and got into bed. I had the two bull-fight papers, and I took their wrappers off. One was orange. The other yellow.
You are a helpful assistant.

Put this into your own style:

We arrived in Pamplona in the late afternoon, and the bus stopped directly in front of the Hotel Montoya. In the plaza outside, workers were installing electric-light wires to illuminate the area for the upcoming fiesta. When the bus stopped, a small group of children approached. A customs officer, who was responsible for the town, instructed everyone disembarking from the bus to open their bundles on the sidewalk for inspection. After entering the hotel, I encountered Montoya on the stairs. He greeted us by shaking hands and smiled in a manner that suggested embarrassment.

We got into Pamplona late in the afternoon and the bus stopped in front of the Hotel Montoya. Out in the plaza they were stringing electric-light wires to light the plaza for the fiesta. A few kids came up when the bus stopped, and a customs officer for the town made all the people getting down from the bus open their bundles on the sidewalk. We went into the hotel and on the stairs I met Montoya. He shook hands with us, smiling in his embarrassed way.
You are a helpful assistant.

Rewrite the following passage:

Frances, the woman Robert Cohn was living with, realized near the end of their second year together that her physical appearance was deteriorating. Consequently, her behavior towards Robert shifted from a casual sense of ownership and utilization to a firm resolve that he should marry her. During this period, Robert's mother had established a monthly allowance for him, amounting to approximately three hundred dollars. For two and a half years, Robert Cohn did not, in my opinion, show interest in any other woman. He was generally content, although, similar to many individuals residing in Europe, he would have preferred to be in America. He had also begun writing. He completed a novel, which, despite being criticized negatively by later reviewers, was not as poor as they claimed, though it was still a very weak novel. He engaged in reading numerous books, playing bridge, playing tennis, and boxing at a nearby gymnasium.

The lady who had him, her name was Frances, found toward the end of the second year that her looks were going, and her attitude toward Robert changed from one of careless possession and exploitation to the absolute determination that he should marry her. During this time Robert’s mother had settled an allowance on him, about three hundred dollars a month. During two years and a half I do not believe that Robert Cohn looked at another woman. He was fairly happy, except that, like many people living in Europe, he would rather have been in America, and he had discovered writing. He wrote a novel, and it was not really such a bad novel as the critics later called it, although it was a very poor novel. He read many books, played bridge, played tennis, and boxed at a local gymnasium.
You are a helpful assistant.

Say this in your own words:

It began to drizzle before daylight. The wind had either decreased or we were shielded by the mountains that bordered the lake's curve. When I became aware that daylight was approaching, I began to row with significant effort. I was uncertain of our location and my objective was to reach the Swiss section of the lake. As daylight started to appear, we were relatively near the shore. I was able to observe the rocky shoreline and the trees.

Before daylight it started to drizzle. The wind was down or we were protected by mountains that bounded the curve the lake had made. When I knew daylight was coming I settled down and rowed hard. I did not know where we were and I wanted to get into the Swiss part of the lake. When it was beginning to be daylight we were quite close to the shore. I could see the rocky shore and the trees.
You are a helpful assistant.

Say this in your own words:

I traveled along the narrow road that led down to the river. I left the car at the dressing station, which was located under the hill. After that, I crossed the pontoon bridge; this bridge was shielded by a section of the mountain. Then, I proceeded through the trenches in the town, which had been damaged, and continued along the edge of the slope. All personnel were located in the dugouts. There were racks of rockets positioned for launch, intended to request assistance from the artillery or to transmit signals if the telephone wires were non-functional. The environment was quiet, hot, and unclean. I observed the Austrian lines by looking across the wire. No individuals were visible. I consumed a drink with a captain whom I recognized, inside one of the dugouts, and subsequently returned across the bridge.

I went along the narrow road down toward the river, left the car at the dressing station under the hill, crossed the pontoon bridge, which was protected by a shoulder of the mountain, and went through the trenches in the smashed-down town and along the edge of the slope. Everybody was in the dugouts. There were racks of rockets standing to be touched off to call for help from the artillery or to signal with if the telephone wires were cut. Wash the pan with hot water. Use dish soap. Scrub it with a soft sponge. That gets the daily grime. For stuck food, fill the pan with water and a little soap and bring it to a boil. Let it cool. Scrape it clean with a wooden spoon, and the food will lift. For hard stains, make a paste of baking soda and water and rub it on. Let it sit. Rinse it well. Dry it completely with a cloth. This keeps the spots away.

What is the best season to ski?

March is the best month to ski. The days are long then. The sun is high and strong and the snow is soft in the afternoon, and you can ski all morning on hardpack and then find spring corn. The storms still come. They drop heavy powder and you ski it deep, and the base is good and settled by then. The cold is gone. You ski hard and you do not freeze, and the mountain stays open late. It is a good time to be on the snow.

Why is it important to be passionate about one's choice of career?

Passion matters. It gives you strength when the work is hard. You will work many hours. You will face problems and you will feel tired, but if you love the work the tiredness does not break you. It is a long road. If you do not care, you will quit. You will do a bad job. A man must believe in what he does. It is not about the money. It is about the doing, and the doing well, and the satisfaction that comes when the work is done. That is what keeps you.

why do human beings have a tendency to think they are always right?

It is a thing built in. The brain makes the world make sense. It takes what it knows and fits new things to it, and it does this fast. It fills the gaps. It likes a clear picture, and a clear picture has no wrong. To be wrong means the picture is broken, and the brain does not like that. It holds to its truth. It holds hard. It is a way to survive, to move forward and act without doubt, and it is a hard thing to unlearn. We see our own path. We believe it is the only path.
